correctness.rationale: Reconstructed RESULT.md lines 23–66 under the stated C², positive-curvature and zero-residual-minimum assumptions. The objective is coercive and strictly convex on the nonempty closed box of differences. For each possible active-edge pattern the free level of a consecutive block is determined by an unconstrained scalar first-order equation; unmarked edges have strict slack, so the actual fit agrees with one of these finitely many maps. Its derivative on a block is an average with strictly positive normalized masses m_i φ_i″. A one-jump input is sent to a nondecreasing vector taking values in [0,1]; the expansion in one-jump inputs plus a constant yields the adjacent-TV bound for every block derivative. Integration gives it for each branch. The fit is continuous by coercivity and comparison; at each segment point a nearby representing branch must coincide there with the fit, by finiteness and continuity. This gives the local centered bound and hence the global bound by the scalar upper right Dini-derivative inequality. To see that inequality, subtract a line of slope strictly above the derivative bound; if its adjusted endpoint value increased, an absolute minimum would occur before the right endpoint, contrary to strict right decrease at a minimum. For power losses the proposed smoothing has strictly positive second derivative, converges uniformly on compact sets, and is bounded below by |t|^p−1 for 0<δ≤1, giving uniformly bounded minimizers by comparison with a fixed feasible vector. The sharpness witnesses are feasible inputs differing by one step across a positive-width edge; if all widths vanish the output difference is constant. The uploaded verify.py was statically inspected, not run; its finite checks are diagnostic only.

evidence: For the nonlinear fitted pair u=T(x), v=T(y), set α_i=m_iφ_i′(u_i−x_i), β_i=m_iφ_i′(v_i−y_i). By strict increase, there is a positive diagonal D with α−β=D[(u−x)−(v−y)]: take coordinate secant slopes, and any positive entry if the two residuals agree. This applies directly also to |·|^p for every p>1.

Set X=u−D⁻¹α and Y=v−D⁻¹β. The nonlinear optimality conditions −α∈N_C(u), −β∈N_C(v) are exactly the optimality conditions for the D-mass quadratic projections of X and Y onto C. Also X−Y=x−y identically.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The previously catalogued all-masses quadratic bound now gives V(u−v)≤V(X−Y)=V(x−y) in one step, with no branch or smoothness approximation needed. When all slope bands are singletons, all fitted differences are constant; otherwise two feasible vectors differing by a small one-edge step attain 1 because the losses minimize at zero. These elementary equality cases exhaust the coefficient. Thus the smooth and independent-power claims are consequences of the operative quadratic theorem, not only analogous special cases.

value.rationale: As a mathematical statement, the exact two-input adjacent-variation law is a useful stability bound for local slope constraints under changing data, including highly heterogeneous losses and fixed edges. It needs no uniform curvature control or bound on the data, distinguishes constrained rigidity from attainable unit sensitivity, and concerns a different norm from the usual fidelity norm. That usefulness does not supply a distinct result once the all-masses quadratic implication is accounted for.
